source_en: Home after the morning mine shift.
Collecting eastern apartments' coal allocation.
End of shift, Coal Face B.
East shaft sealed this morning. Home.
Collecting protective gear from the depot.
Double shift at C shaft. Sleep.
Every mine is closed. Just home.
Nowhere else to go. Mine's shut.
Home to the east block. Wife waits.
Textile mill clerk. Home for lunch.
First wage packet. Started at the mine Monday.
Home to an empty flat. Never married.
Starting my east shaft shift. Coal Face B.
University entrance exam. Mining engineering.
Visiting my sons east. I live west.
The mine runs fine. Back underground now.
Retired ten years ago. Visiting the crew.
The foreman called my name. Back down.
Long shift. Just off the morning rotation, Coal Face B. Papers in order.
I know I'm dirty. The showers at the shaft were out again.
They moved us to C shaft. Longer walk. Worse air.
Eleven hours today. The ventilation has been bad. I don't complain.
They closed the mine. I don't know what I'm supposed to do now.
I used to know what my day was. Just going home.
Good. Thank you, officer. Going home now.
Right. Thank you. Back to the bunk.
Alright. Nothing to go back to anyway.
I've slept in mine shafts tighter than this. I'll manage.
Concrete, not rock. But it's the same in the dark.
Thirty years underground... gas pockets... collapses... and this...
I thought... it would be the mine... that got me...
Where are you coming from?
Coal Face B, east shaft. Morning rotation. Going home to the east block.
C shaft. They sealed the east one. Eleven hours. Longer walk home.
Nowhere. The mine is shut. I stood at the gate a while.
The tram depot. I drive the number four line. Twelve years now.
Coal Face B, east shaft. Same as always. Nothing to report.
The station. Wife left on the Tbilisi train. I live alone now.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Coal dust. Always coal dust. The mine doctor says my lungs are fine.
Some dizziness. Ventilation in C shaft is bad. It passes. Mostly.
Tired. More than usual. No sleep without the shift. Same cough.
Nothing. I am thirty-one. The body does not complain yet.
Nothing. C shaft has the best air in the mine. New fans.
Never coughed in my life. I kept the office ledgers. Never went down.
B shaft today. Long one. Papers are in order. Always are.
I know I smell. The showers at the mine were out again.
Three men on my crew did not show this morning. Nobody said anything.
I do not complain. I just want to get through the week.
The mine is closed. First time in thirty years I have nothing to go back to.
Just going home. That is all there is now.
